catalog_quote: present a reconstruction of Proto Seko phonology on the basis of data from four closely related languages in northern South Sulawesi (Seko Padang, Seko Tengah, Panasuan, and Budong-budong), based on several years of fieldwork in this area. ... The common basic elements of the phonology of Seko languages are stated in the following list. ... 7. Stress is penultimate. ... 8. Closed syllables are common. Closed syllable structure is maintained when adding stress-shifting suffixes. ... 10. Possessive suffixes, which all begin with consonants and are stress-shifting, only attach to stem-final codas. ... VOWEL LENGTH occurs in word final position, where it is contrastive. Length can occur on any of the five vowels. Word stress does not shift, but remains penultimate. ... VOWEL QUICKNESS is contrastive only in the stressed syllable (penultimate position).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word in all four Seko languages, Panasuan explicitly included. Contrastive word-final long vowels do not attract stress (it stays on the penult). Stress is computed on the suffixed word: consonant-initial possessive suffixes and nominalizing -ang are 'stress-shifting' (stress moves to the new penult, e.g. Seko Padang ming-kutik-i 'ask' vs ping-kutìk-ang 'question', p. 4), whereas the echo vowel -i in Seko Padang is 'non-stress-shifting'. Quick (reduced, schwa-like) vowels are contrastive only in the stressed penult.
new_statements.exceptions: None for root words; final long vowels explicitly do not shift stress; suffixation shifts stress with 'stress-shifting' suffixes (possessives, -ang) but not with the non-stress-shifting echo vowel -i (Seko Padang example).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (roots and suffixed words). The statement is made for the Seko subgroup as a whole on the basis of the author's fieldwork in all four languages; the illustrative examples are Seko Padang and Seko Tengah, none is Panasuan. No phrase-level or citation-form remarks.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is made for the Seko subgroup collectively (Glottolog seko1241: Seko Padang seko1242, Seko Tengah, Panasuan pana1303, Budong-Budong budo1241) as 'common basic elements of the phonology of Seko languages', with Panasuan explicitly among the four languages the author worked on; the illustrative examples are Seko Padang and Seko Tengah, not Panasuan. Only Panasuan-specific segmental note in the source: /c/ is an allophone of /t/ before high vowels (p. 2). No dialect of Panasuan is distinguished.
